title: When Sentiment Scores Lie: Lessons from Analysing Political Twitter
summary: Pre-trained sentiment models trained on product reviews fail systematically on political discourse. Here is what I learned retraining on domain-specific data.

blocks.text: When I first applied a standard VADER sentiment analyser to a corpus of political tweets, the accuracy looked reasonable—until I checked the errors. The model consistently rated aggressive political rhetoric as neutral and labelled ironic criticism as positive.

Most off-the-shelf sentiment models are trained on Amazon product reviews or IMDB ratings. Political discourse has a fundamentally different lexicon: words like austeridad, recortes, or a politician's surname carry strong valence that a product-review model has never seen in a polarised context.
I fine-tuned a multilingual BERT model on 4 000 manually annotated political tweets. The fine-tuned model improved macro-F1 from 0.48 to 0.81 on the held-out test set.
Domain adaptation matters more than model size. A fine-tuned BERT-base outperformed GPT-3.5 zero-shot on this task by 12 percentage points, at a fraction of the cost.
